seoDescription: Learn the fundamentals of Odoo inventory management with this comprehensive step-by-step tutorial. This guide walks you through setting up your Odoo account, adding your first products, and managing stock levels. Discover how to process receipts from suppliers, create and validate delivery orders for customers or internal transfers, and track physical inventory counts to identify and resolve discrepancies. Master key operations like managing product details, prices, and quantities to streamline your entire inventory workflow.

summary:
## Getting Started with Odoo Inventory

To begin using Odoo for inventory management, you need to create and activate your account:
1.  Navigate to **odoo.com** and select the **Inventory** app.
2.  Click **"Start now, it's free"** and fill out the registration form with your name, email, and company details.
3.  Check your email for an activation link to verify your account.
4.  Create a secure password and activate your Odoo database.

## Core Inventory Operations

Once your dashboard is active, you can manage your inventory through several key functions.

### Adding Products

Create new items in your inventory catalog by clicking **Products > New Product**.

-   **Product Type**: Choose between **Storable**, **Consumable**, or **Service**.
-   **Pricing**: Set a **Sale Price** and **Cost Price** to track profitability.
-   **Categorization**: Assign a **Product Category** (e.g., 'Salable') and add internal references or barcodes.

> [!TIP]
> After creating a product, use the **Update Quantity** button to set the initial number of units you have on hand in your stock.

### Processing Receipts (Incoming Stock)

Log items you are receiving from suppliers.

1.  Go to **Operations > Receipts** and click **New**.
2.  Select or create a **Contact** for the supplier.
3.  Add product lines, specifying the **Demanded** quantity for each item.
4.  Set a **Scheduled Date** for the expected arrival.
5.  Click **Mark as To Do** to formalize the receipt.

### Managing Deliveries (Outgoing Stock)

Create orders for products being sent out to customers or other locations.

1.  Go to **Operations > Delivery Orders** and click **New**.
2.  Select or create a destination **Contact** (e.g., a customer or another store).
3.  Add the product and the **Demanded** quantity being sent.
4.  Once the order is ready to ship, click **Validate** to confirm the items have been dispatched, marking the operation as complete.

## Advanced Operations & Reconciliation

### Physical Inventory

This feature is crucial for maintaining accurate stock records.

-   It allows you to compare the system's **Quantity on Hand** with the physically **Counted Quantity**.
-   The **Difference** field highlights discrepancies between what the system expects and what is actually in your warehouse.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use the discrepancy data to investigate stock losses or receiving errors and resolve them with your suppliers.

## Getting Started with Odoo

Odoo Inventory management tutorial step by step. Hello everyone, welcome back. In this video, I'll show you guys how you can get started with inventory management using Odoo. So let's jump right in.

Now, Odoo is a tool that has multiple different segmentations and a software that can be diversified into a larger ecosystem as well. So if you're just looking for inventory management or looking for much more, Odoo has solutions for all. Now, if you're looking to get started with your own tool with just Inventory management, simply go on to odoo.com and scroll down and click on inventory. From there, you will be able to use the inventory management tool separately.

Click on 'Start now, it's free' to get started for free using Odoo. Now over here, you're going to have instant access to Odoo's tool. Simply type in your first and last name, then type in your email address like so, add your company name, and then add your phone number, primary interest, and company size to proceed. Once you have completed your sign up, you will have an activation email sent. So simply open up your mailbox and verify your account on Odoo to proceed with Odoo's inventory management tool. Click on 'activate your dashboard' to be able to access all the features of Odoo.

Now from here, you're going to have to create a suitable password for your Odoo account, and you need to make sure that it is eight characters. Click on 'Activate database' over here to activate your Odoo database.

## Navigating the Inventory Dashboard

Now that our Odoo database is activated, we can proceed with our colleagues. So we can invite more colleagues or skip this step for now. Click on 'Go to Odoo' and then click on 'Inventory'. Once you click on inventory, you will see an inventory overview. Now over here you have the option to link menu and spreadsheet and create an inventory flow from your spreadsheets. So you can click on your inventory overview to get started with putting in inventory items.

Now on the top, you have the option to view different receipts as well. So you can go into your receipts processes to view your processes in inventory, and then your delivery orders to view delivery orders. You can take a look at your overview, different operations such as physical inventory, scrap, procurement, as well as receipts and deliveries.

## Adding Your First Product

Click on 'Product' on the top right to first add your product. So you will click on 'New Product' on the top left. Once you click on new products, you can add your first product. Let's say for us this is going to be our 'YouTube Logo Tee'. Then you can add general information about the product, whether it is a consumable product, whether it is a service, or whether it is a storable product. So let's say this is going to be a storable product. 

Below that, we can add our sale price, so let's say it's $88, and then our cost price as well. Adding sale and cost prices can help us in managing our profits and losses with Odoo as well.

Below that we also have our product category, whether this is an expense, salable, or you can even add your own customized product category. For us, this is a salable product, which means that it is going to be sold. We can add an internal reference code, a barcode, and we can also add a product template tag that we might be using in our pre-existing software systems. Then you can also add internal notes, and once completed, your product will be created.

Now on the top, you can click on Extra Prices, Documents, On Hand, Forecasted, and In and Out, and Reordering Rules. Click on 'Update Quantity' over here to update the quantity. So let's say I have 50,000 units in stock. Click on Apply over here. You can click on 'Print Labels' to start printing labels with the price as well. Now, once you have completed this, you can proceed with your next function.

## Processing Incoming Receipts

Which is going to be building your receipts and deliverables. So these are different operations. You can click on 'New Receipt' on the top left to add a receipt. Let's say I am supposed to receive from a new supplier, so I can go on ahead and create a new contact over here. So I can go on ahead and go into 'New' and then create a new contact which is going to be maybe RAKK Print and then I can add more info but I will just click on 'Save and Close'. 

And I'm supposed to receive, let's say I will add a line, a new product which is going to be called our 'Minimal' or, let's say this is going to be called our 'Zoo Print T-shirt' like this. And after that I can add the demand that I have for the product that I want to receive. So let's say I want to receive 30 units just as a tester. Let's say I want to receive 2,000 units just as a tester for my stores. Then once completed I can go on ahead and add a scheduled date. So let's say I am supposed to receive these in around two weeks, um, let's say over here. And I can also add a source document.

Once done, I can click on 'Mark as To Do' on the top left. I can also click on 'Send a Message' to send a message to people following this particular operation. You can also click on 'Print' and 'Print Labels' to send this particular receipt out. So if I want, I can configure this document and send this out as a document in the mailbox.

## Creating and Validating Delivery Orders

Below that you can pretty much do the same thing for your delivery. So if you are supposed to receive a delivery, you can add your delivery address if it's for you or if it's for the other business. You can add your product as well. So for our delivery address, I will create a new contact, which might be my own store. So this is going to be 'Lily's Bradford store' like this. And this is going to be a company, let's say, and I can click on 'Save and Close' over here.

And then I can add a line product, which might be my pre-existing product. So I will add my 'YouTube Logo Tee' and I'm going to be sending out 6,000 units of that like so. Click on over here and click on 'Mark as To Do'. Now it's ready, and I can click on 'Done' over here. So when my task is completed, I can mark it as done. So if I go back into my deliveries, I say it is ready. I can click on 'Validate' on the top left and validate that this has been sent and received. And now this is going to be a completed operation in Odoo's Inventory management system.

## Managing Physical Inventory and Conclusion

I can also go into managing my operations with physical inventory and scraps. Your physical inventory will show you the quantity on hand, counted quantity, any difference. So if you logged in that you received 10,000 units of a product but later on when you actually viewed it, you would notice that you only received 9,500 products. So you can manage the difference and make sure to clear that with your suppliers. 

And just like that, you can get started with Odoo's inventory management. If you found this video helpful, make sure to leave a like and subscribe to our YouTube channel. And if you have any questions about Odoo, about any other tool regarding inventory management, CRM, sales, marketing, or anything at all, make sure to leave that in the comment box down below. I would love to help you guys out and know what you guys have to say. And if you enjoyed this video, make sure to leave a like, subscribe, and comment down below, and I will catch you guys in the next video.
